question: The average weight (in kg) of a family of five members, whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 74 kg, and 39 kg, is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the assumed average be 50 kg.

Deviations from 50: (40 − 50) = −10, (49 − 50) = −1, (56 − 50) = +6, (74 − 50) = +24, (39 − 50) = −11.

Net deviation = −10 − 1 + 6 + 24 − 11 = +8

Average deviation = 8 ÷ 5 = +1.6 kg

Actual Average = Assumed Average + Average Deviation = 50 + 1.6 = 51.6 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 51.6 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Weights of family members = 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 74 kg, and 39 kg

Total number of members = 5

 Weights of Family Members (in kg)

**Formula Used:**

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of weights = 40 + 49 + 56 + 74 + 39

⇒ Sum of weights = 258 kg

⇒ Average = 258 ÷ 5

⇒ Average = 51.6 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 51.6 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

When two or more groups have different averages, their combined average is calculated as: Combined Average = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

Deviation Method

It simplifies average calculations by choosing an assumed mean (A). The actual average = A + (Sum of deviations ÷ Total items).

Effect of Arithmetic Operations

If a constant value is added, subtracted, multiplied or divided to each given observation, the new average will similarly undergo the exact same arithmetic operation with that constant.
